aircraft: Generic X-Plane 12 default GA radio stack
label: X-Plane 12 default COM/NAV/ADF/DME/XPDR radio stack
description: Dataref/command mapping for a generic COM1/COM2/NAV1/NAV2/ADF/DME/XPDR radio panel, confirmed live against a running X-Plane 12.4.3 with the stock Beechcraft King Air C90 (ICAO B9L) loaded (2026-08-11). Everything here lives under the plain sim/radios, sim/audio_panel, and sim/transponder namespaces (not laminar/c90/...), which is X-Plane's own generic radio-stack implementation shared across its default GA aircraft the same way the default FMS/CDU is (see b738-fms.json) — expected to generalize to other default aircraft with the standard radio stack, but re-verify before trusting unchanged; add-on aircraft with custom avionics won't have any of this. Verified live: com1's coarse/fine standby-tune commands step the standby frequency by the expected amount, its flip command cleanly swaps active<->standby, the ADF hundreds_thous/ones_tens commands (per explicit confirmation, not a guess) step the standby ADF frequency correctly, and the transponder_12/34_up/down commands step the expected digit pairs of the squawk code.
_note_on_xpdr_mode: Deliberately not wired yet — transponder_mode is a live-confirmed 8-state enum (off=0, standby=1, on=2, alt=3, test=4, ground=5, ta_only=6, ta_ra=7), not the simple ON/OFF the panel brief calls for. Add once it's decided how that collapses.
_note_on_xpdr_audio: No XPDR entry in the audio-toggle row — transponders don't have an audio channel to monitor in X-Plane's model (no sim/audio_panel/monitor_audio_xpdr-shaped command exists), unlike the other six radios.
_note_on_com_833: COM1/COM2 use the _833 (8.33kHz-spacing) dataref variants, not the plain 25kHz ones — confirmed live these give 3 decimal digits of real precision (e.g. 118.505), matching the display's 6-digit/3-decimal format; the plain variants only carry 2. NAV/DME have no _833 variant (fixed 50kHz spacing) — the plain dataref's 2 real decimal digits are shown padded with a trailing 0 to fill the same 6-digit/3-decimal window, no precision lost since a 50kHz-spaced value is always exactly .x0 or .x5.
_note_on_standby_tuning: The standby frequency actuators are directly writable (confirmed live 2026-08-11: setting com1_standby_frequency_hz_833/nav1_standby_frequency_hz/dme_standby_frequency_hz/adf1_standby_frequency_hz all took immediately, no override-back from the sim), so standby tuning uses each readout's own `encoder` (writeDataref pointing at the same standby dataref, valueKey "standby") via EfisAdapter.adjustReadoutValue()/beginAdjust()/endAdjust() — the same pattern the FCU/EFIS baro knob already uses. An earlier version instead fired the discrete stby_*_coarse/fine_up/down step commands (still present under XPDR below, which has no writable dataref), paced to dodge X-Plane's command_set_is_active coalescing (activations spaced closer than its ~150ms hold duration collapse into one) — that turned out to be the wrong tool for a fast knob drag: even generously paced, a burst of rapid presses reliably lost steps (confirmed live: 10 rapid stby_com1_fine_up_833 presses sometimes landed as few as 4-5 real steps, one burst even produced a net *negative* delta), and a fast drag would queue far more presses than could drain before the display needed to settle. A direct write has no hold-duration/coalescing concept at all, so src/radio-panel.js computes the real per-press step size itself (see _note_on_step_sizes) and writes the new standby value directly — no queue, no pacing.
_note_on_step_sizes: Real per-press step sizes, confirmed live 2026-08-11 by firing each step command once in isolation and reading the resulting dataref delta: COM1/COM2 coarse=1000 (1MHz) fine=5 (0.005MHz, i.e. true 8.33kHz-ish spacing — NOT the naive 25 (0.025MHz/25kHz) a 25kHz-spacing assumption would give). NAV1/NAV2/DME coarse=100 (1MHz, remember these datarefs carry only 2 decimal digits) fine=5 (0.05MHz/50kHz). ADF coarse=100 (100kHz, the hundreds_thous digit pair) fine=1 (1kHz, the ones_tens digit pair). Real 2-ring radios keep the fine (kHz) ring and coarse (MHz) ring independent of each other — confirmed live 2026-08-11 the real fine_up_833/stby_nav1_fine_up commands wrap the sub-MHz offset back to its own decade's start without ever touching the MHz digit, and the coarse commands wrap the MHz digit around at the band edges (136.500 coarse-up -> 118.500) while leaving the kHz offset untouched, rather than hard-stopping. COM's real 8.33kHz grid isn't a uniform every-5 sequence within a decade either — it skips one value every 25 raw units (the real ICAO 8.33kHz-within-legacy-25kHz-block channel numbering) and the valid range per decade is 0-990, not 0-975 as this profile originally assumed (copied uncritically from the vendored component's own BANDS table, which was simply wrong — walking the real command through a full decade live disproved it). All of this is reproduced exactly in src/radio-panel.js's nextStandbyRaw() (cross-validated live against the real commands with zero mismatches across 36 test cases spanning both wrap cases and ADF's edge-clamping) — that function, not this note, is the source of truth.

readouts.name: MIC_SEL
readouts._note: audio_com_selection isn't a clean 0/1 enum -- confirmed live 2026-08-12 it read 6 for COM1 and 7 for COM2 in this session (other bits already set by the aircraft's own baseline state). src/radio-panel.js reads this by parity (odd = COM2, even = COM1) rather than an exact-match toggle, since the baseline pair could plausibly shift with other audio-panel state a strict enum match wouldn't tolerate. transmit_audio_com1/com2 are one-shot select commands, not toggles -- deliberately not the _man variants (X-Plane's own description: "old panel, doesn't change listener").
